text: SUBJECT Unresolved biological-unit imbalance following April inventory reconciliation. CONTEXT The monthly reconciliation reviewed receipts, declared internal use, documented waste, adjustments, and outbound records for the controlled biological-sample category. Adjustment ADJ-2022-00088 was included in the review. Unit conversions were checked against the current item master. FINDINGS The opening balance and posted receipts reconcile with the warehouse ledger. Declared internal use and waste are supported by signed records. The outbound register accounts for the listed shipments, but the calculated closing balance remains above the physical count. A recount by a second controller produced the same result. No temperature excursion or damaged-container report explains the difference. The discrepancy is concentrated in sealed biological units handled under restricted authorization. Similar differences have occurred in earlier periods, although their direction and size vary. Ordinary causes such as delayed posting, split batches, unit conversion, and transfer between storage locations remain under review. ACTION Maintain the adjustment as provisional, suspend automatic closure of the period, and obtain the secure dispatch register for comparison. This memorandum establishes a material sink in the accounting sequence; it does not identify a destination, user, or purpose.

SCOPE This instruction applies to staff handling secure delivery records associated with shipment SHP-2022-00011 and related restricted consignments. CONTROL REQUIREMENTS Records marked CHAMELEO are to be routed through the designated compliance queue. Staff must verify the receiving facility code, named authorization class, seal number, and temperature-control record before release. Copies are not to be attached to ordinary customer correspondence. Route changes require approval from the security manager and the duty compliance officer. RESPONSIBILITIES Operations staff retain the ordinary shipment record. Security staff retain the sealed routing appendix. Warehouse staff record only the declared cargo category and quantity in the standard inventory system. Any mismatch between the standard record and the restricted appendix must be escalated rather than corrected locally. ESCALATION Contact the secure-delivery desk for missing signatures, unexplained destination changes, or requests to bypass the receiving scan. The code identifies a handling and governance procedure. This instruction does not explain the programme's wider purpose, the ownership of the designation, or the final use of any cargo.

MEETING RECORD — RESTRICTED GOVERNANCE REVIEW Attendees included the executive chair, the secure-delivery manager, clinical programme counsel, and the records secretary. AGENDA 1. Authority for CHAMELEO routing. 2. Relationship between programme designation and executive approvals. 3. Separation of ordinary corporate records from restricted appendices. DISCUSSION The chair confirmed that Unwabu is the designation used in the restricted governance schedule for the authority approving CHAMELEO exceptions. The same schedule assigns final escalation to the Meridian executive office. Participants agreed that ordinary employees should see only shipment, inventory, and compliance fields needed for their roles. The secretary noted that earlier instructions treated CHAMELEO as a handling code, while the governance schedule links it to a named authority. DECISIONS The secure-delivery manager will maintain the restricted appendix. Compliance will retain a cross-reference between the designation, executive approvals, and affected routes. No change will be made to public corporate filings. LIMITS This record establishes an Unwabu–CHAMELEO–Meridian authority bridge. The meeting did not review other networks, biological questions, ecological material, or destination records. The chair instructed staff not to alter existing operational records retrospectively. Any reconciliation should be recorded as a new governance note with a visible date and responsible role. The meeting did not review ecological evidence or clinical files, and participants were reminded that their authority was limited to routing and programme governance.
